inlines.text: Jacob is making a drink using cordial and water.
For every one part cordial, he uses four parts water.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the ratio of cordial to water.

answer.worked: There is 1 part cordial for every 4 parts water, so cordial : water $=1:4$.

inlines.text: Jacob makes a second drink using cordial to water in the ratio
Will this drink be stronger or weaker than his first drink?

answer.short: Weaker: there is more water for each part of cordial.
answer.worked: The first drink has 4 parts water for each part of cordial; the second has 5. The second drink is weaker because it has more water for the same amount of cordial.

inlines.text: Which of these ratios of cordial to water will make the strongest drink?

answer.worked:
Compare cordial as a fraction of water:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}&=\frac{6}{30}\\\frac{2}{5}&=\frac{12}{30}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{20}{30}\\\frac{3}{10}&=\frac{9}{30}\end{aligned}$$
The largest fraction is $\frac{2}{3}$, so $2:3$ gives the most cordial for the same amount of water and makes the strongest drink.

inlines.text: Jenny says that there must also be more of the second drink compared to the first drink.
Explain why she is not correct.

answer.short: A ratio compares the amounts of cordial and water; it does not give the total amount of drink.
answer.worked: The ratios give the relative amounts of cordial and water, but the size of one part is not stated. The second drink could therefore have a smaller, equal or larger total amount.

answer.worked:
The lowest common denominator is $12$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4}&=\frac{5\times3}{4\times3}=\frac{15}{12}\\\frac{1}{3}&=\frac{1\times4}{3\times4}=\frac{4}{12}\end{aligned}$$

The lowest common denominator is $15$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}&=\frac{4\times3}{5\times3}=\frac{12}{15}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{2\times5}{3\times5}=\frac{10}{15}\end{aligned}$$

The lowest common denominator is $6$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{2\times2}{3\times2}=\frac{4}{6}\\\frac{5}{6}&=\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{align*}100:28:4&=(100\div4):(28\div4):(4\div4)\\&=25:7:1\end{align*}$$

Multiply both parts by $10$ to obtain whole numbers.
$$\begin{align*}1.6:1.9&=(1.6\times10):(1.9\times10)\\&=16:19\end{align*}$$
The highest common factor is $1$.

Multiply both parts by $100$, then divide by the highest common factor, $3$.
$$\begin{align*}0.93:0.6&=93:60\\&=(93\div3):(60\div3)\\&=31:20\end{align*}$$

Write the mixed number as an improper fraction. Both fractions have denominator $2$, so multiply both parts by $2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3}{2}:2\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{3}{2}:\frac{5}{2}\\&=\left(\frac{3}{2}\times2\right):\left(\frac{5}{2}\times2\right)\\&=3:5\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: $2.2\text{ kg}:850\text{ g}$

answer.worked:
$2.2\text{ kg}=2200\text{ g}$. Compare in grams, then divide both parts by $50$.
$$\begin{align*}2200:850&=(2200\div50):(850\div50)\\&=44:17\end{align*}$$

children.label: g
children.prompt: $6\text{ min}:2.1\text{ h}$

answer.worked:
$2.1\text{ h}=2.1\times60\text{ min}=126\text{ min}$. Compare in minutes, then divide both parts by $6$.
$$\begin{align*}6:126&=(6\div6):(126\div6)\\&=1:21\end{align*}$$

Rewrite with lowest common denominator $6$, then multiply both parts by $6$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{2}:\frac{1}{3}&=\frac{3}{6}:\frac{2}{6}\\&=\left(\frac{3}{6}\times6\right):\left(\frac{2}{6}\times6\right)\\&=3:2\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: $25\text{ cm}:1.1\text{ m}$

answer.worked:
$1.1\text{ m}=110\text{ cm}$. Compare in centimetres, then divide both parts by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}25:110&=(25\div5):(110\div5)\\&=5:22\end{align*}$$

$\$1.50=150\text{ c}$. Compare in cents, then divide both parts by $10$.
$$\begin{align*}150:80&=(150\div10):(80\div10)\\&=15:8\end{align*}$$

children.label: k
children.prompt: $600\text{ mL}:1.5\text{ L}$

answer.worked:
$1.5\text{ L}=1500\text{ mL}$. Compare in millilitres, then divide both parts by $300$.
$$\begin{align*}600:1500&=(600\div300):(1500\div300)\\&=2:5\end{align*}$$

Rewrite with lowest common denominator $24$, then multiply both parts by $24$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{5}{8}:\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{15}{24}:\frac{16}{24}\\&=\left(\frac{15}{24}\times24\right):\left(\frac{16}{24}\times24\right)\\&=15:16\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
$0.6\text{ m}=600\text{ mm}$ and $15\text{ cm}=150\text{ mm}$.

$$\begin{align*}15\text{ cm}:0.6\text{ m}:30\text{ mm}&=150:600:30\\&=5:20:1\end{align*}$$
Divide every part by $30$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $2\text{ min}:45\text{ s}:1\text{ min }25\text{ s}$

answer.worked:
$2\text{ min}=120\text{ s}$ and $1\text{ min }25\text{ s}=85\text{ s}$.

$$\begin{align*}2\text{ min}:45\text{ s}:1\text{ min }25\text{ s}&=120:45:85\\&=24:9:17\end{align*}$$
Divide every part by $5$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: $1.2\text{ kg}:800\text{ g}:0.4\text{ kg}$

answer.worked:
$1.2\text{ kg}=1200\text{ g}$ and $0.4\text{ kg}=400\text{ g}$.

$$\begin{align*}1.2\text{ kg}:800\text{ g}:0.4\text{ kg}&=1200:800:400\\&=3:2:1\end{align*}$$
Divide every part by $400$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: $600\text{ L}:4.2\text{ kL}:0.9\text{ kL}$

answer.worked:
$4.2\text{ kL}=4200\text{ L}$ and $0.9\text{ kL}=900\text{ L}$.

$$\begin{align*}600\text{ L}:4.2\text{ kL}:0.9\text{ kL}&=600:4200:900\\&=2:14:3\end{align*}$$
Divide every part by $300$.

children.label: f
children.prompt: $3\text{ weeks}:1\text{ fortnight}$

answer.worked:
$3\text{ weeks}=21\text{ days}$ and $1\text{ fortnight}=14\text{ days}$.

$$\begin{align*}3\text{ weeks}:1\text{ fortnight}&=21:14\\&=3:2\end{align*}$$
Divide both parts by $7$.

children.label: g
children.prompt: $6000\text{ mg}:12\text{ g}:0.06\text{ kg}$

answer.worked:
$12\text{ g}=12000\text{ mg}$ and $0.06\text{ kg}=60000\text{ mg}$.

$$\begin{align*}6000\text{ mg}:12\text{ g}:0.06\text{ kg}&=6000:12000:60000\\&=1:2:10\end{align*}$$
Divide every part by $6000$.

$1\text{ cm}^{2}=100\text{ mm}^{2}$, so $10\text{ cm}^{2}=1000\text{ mm}^{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}10\text{ cm}^{2}:200\text{ mm}^{2}&=1000:200\\&=5:1\end{align*}$$
Divide both parts by $200$.

$1\text{ ha}=10000\text{ m}^{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}600\text{ m}^{2}:1\text{ ha}&=600:10000\\&=3:50\end{align*}$$
Divide both parts by $200$.

spec.description: A 10 cm by 5 cm outer rectangle contains a shaded 4 cm by 2 cm rectangle toward the lower-left.
spec.mathematics: Outer area 50 cm²; shaded area 8 cm²; remaining area 42 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions are visible; calculated areas and ratios belong to answers.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=4\times2=8\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{whole}}&=10\times5=50\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=50-8=42\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $2$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=8:42\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=4:21\end{align*}$

spec.description: A 20 cm by 15 cm rectangle contains two separate shaded triangles, pointing upward at lower-left and downward at upper-right. Their shared base and height annotation remains to the right.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle has base 10 cm and height 9 cm, giving total shaded area 90 cm² and remaining area 210 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions and shared triangle annotation remain visible; calculated areas and ratios are answers.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{one triangle}}&=\frac12\times10\times9=45\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=2\times45=90\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{whole}}&=20\times15=300\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=300-90=210\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $30$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=90:210\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=3:7\end{align*}$

spec.description: A smaller unshaded circle is offset upward inside a larger shaded circle. Separate centre markers identify the smaller circle's upper-right radius and the larger circle's downward radius.
spec.mathematics: The smaller radius is 4 cm and the larger radius is 8 cm. The centres are distinct; the shaded area is the difference of the two circle areas.
spec.answerVisibility: The two radii and centre markers remain visible; area calculations and ratios are answers.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{large circle}}&=\pi\times8^2=64\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=\pi\times4^2=16\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=64\pi-16\pi=48\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $16\pi$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=48\pi:16\pi\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=3:1\end{align*}$

spec.description: A circle has two white upper sectors labelled 30° and 50°. The remaining region, including the lower semicircle and the central upper sector, is shaded. All source radii and both angle arcs are retained.
spec.mathematics: Unshaded central angles total 80°; shaded central angles total 280°. Areas in the same circle are proportional to their central angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 30° and 50° labels appear; totals and ratios belong to answers.

answer.worked:
Sector areas in the same circle are proportional to their central angles.
$\begin{align*}\theta_{\text{unshaded}}&=30^\circ+50^\circ=80^\circ\\\theta_{\text{shaded}}&=360^\circ-80^\circ=280^\circ\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $40$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=280:80\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=7:2\end{align*}$

answer.short:

answer.worked:
Both triangles have height $2\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}

\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:

\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: A drink is made by mixing water and cordial in the ratio $5:2$.

inlines.text: How much cordial do you need for 200 mL of water?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}5\text{ parts}&=200\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=(200\div5)\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=40\text{ mL}\\2\text{ parts}&=(40\times2)\text{ mL}\\2\text{ parts}&=80\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
You need 80 mL of cordial.

inlines.text: How much water do you need for 60 mL of cordial?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=60\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=(60\div2)\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=30\text{ mL}\\5\text{ parts}&=(30\times5)\text{ mL}\\5\text{ parts}&=150\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
You need 150 mL of water.

inlines.text: How much drink, in total, can you make with 120 mL of cordial?

answer.worked:
The total drink represents $5+2=7$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=120\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=(120\div2)\text{ mL}\\1\text{ part}&=60\text{ mL}\\7\text{ parts}&=(60\times7)\text{ mL}\\7\text{ parts}&=420\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
You can make 420 mL of drink.

children.label: a

There are 12 apples.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Apples : bananas $=3:5$.
There are 35 bananas.
Find the number of apples.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}5\text{ parts}&=35\text{ bananas}\\1\text{ part}&=35\div5=7\text{ fruits}\\3\text{ parts}&=3\times7=21\text{ apples}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Apples : bananas $=3:5$.
There are 12 apples.
Find the total number of fruits.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}3\text{ parts}&=12\text{ apples}\\1\text{ part}&=12\div3=4\text{ fruits}\\\text{Total parts}&=3+5=8\\8\text{ parts}&=8\times4=32\text{ fruits}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt:
Apples : bananas $=3:5$.
There are 35 bananas.

$$\begin{align*}5\text{ parts}&=35\text{ bananas}\\1\text{ part}&=35\div5=7\text{ fruits}\\\text{Difference in parts}&=5-3=2\\2\text{ parts}&=2\times7=14\text{ fruits}\end{align*}$$
There are 14 more bananas than apples.

children.label: e
children.prompt:
Red : blue $=5:2$.
There are 7.5 L of blue paint.
Find the red paint required.

$$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=7.5\text{ L}\\1\text{ part}&=7.5\div2=3.75\text{ L}\\5\text{ parts}&=5\times3.75=18.75\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
18.75 L of red paint is required.

children.label: f
children.prompt:
Boys : girls $=4:7$.
There are 20 boys.
Find the number of girls.

children.label: g

18 m of pine is required.

Bottle B has 1 L of cordial drink with a cordial to water ratio of
The drink from both bottles is combined to form a 2 L drink.
What is the new cordial to water ratio?

answer.worked:
Bottle A has $3+7=10$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}10\text{ parts}&=1\text{ L}\\1\text{ part}&=1\div10=0.1\text{ L}\\\text{Cordial in A}&=3\times0.1=0.3\text{ L}\\\text{Water in A}&=7\times0.1=0.7\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
Bottle B has $1+4=5$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}5\text{ parts}&=1\text{ L}\\1\text{ part}&=1\div5=0.2\text{ L}\\\text{Cordial in B}&=1\times0.2=0.2\text{ L}\\\text{Water in B}&=4\times0.2=0.8\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
Combine the corresponding volumes.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total cordial}&=0.3+0.2=0.5\text{ L}\\\text{Total water}&=0.7+0.8=1.5\text{ L}\\\text{Cordial : water}&=0.5:1.5\\\text{Cordial : water}&=1:3\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Adam, Bertie, and Cameron are sharing \$240. Work out how much each person receives.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Bertie receives \$60. The ratio of Adam’s to Cameron’s shares are $4:5$.

answer.worked:
Adam and Cameron share the remaining money.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Remaining money}&=\$240-\$60\\&=\$180\\\text{Total parts}&=4+5=9\\\text{1 part}&=\$180\div9=\$20\\\text{Adam’s share}&=4\times\$20=\$80\\\text{Cameron’s share}&=5\times\$20=\$100\end{align*}$$
Bertie receives \$60.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Adam receives $\frac{1}{3}$ of the money. The ratio of Bertie to Cameron’s shares are $1:3$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Adam’s share}&=\frac{1}{3}\times\$240\\&=\$80\\\text{Remaining money}&=\$240-\$80\\&=\$160\\\text{Total remaining parts}&=1+3=4\\\text{1 part}&=\$160\div4=\$40\\\text{Bertie’s share}&=\$40\\\text{Cameron’s share}&=3\times\$40=\$120\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Cameron receives $20\%$ more money than Adam. The ratio of Adam to Bertie is $5:1$.

answer.worked:
Adam has 5 parts. Cameron has $20\%$ more, so Cameron has $5+\frac{20}{100}\times5=6$ parts. Thus Adam : Bertie : Cameron is $5:1:6$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=5+1+6=12\\\text{1 part}&=\$240\div12=\$20\\\text{Adam’s share}&=5\times\$20=\$100\\\text{Bertie’s share}&=\$20\\\text{Cameron’s share}&=6\times\$20=\$120\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The ratio of Adam to Bertie’s shares are $1:3$. The ratio of Bertie to Cameron’s shares are $1:2$.

answer.worked:
Match Bertie’s parts: Bertie : Cameron is $1:2=3:6$. Thus Adam : Bertie : Cameron is $1:3:6$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=1+3+6=10\\\text{1 part}&=\$240\div10=\$24\\\text{Adam’s share}&=\$24\\\text{Bertie’s share}&=3\times\$24=\$72\\\text{Cameron’s share}&=6\times\$24=\$144\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: The ratio of students to staff in a school trip is

children.label: a
children.prompt: What are the possible total number of staff and students on the trip?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=25+3\\&=28\end{align*}$$
The total must be a positive whole-number multiple of 28: $28,56,84,\ldots$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: There are 12 members of staff. Some students then cancel. The ratio is now $15:2$. How many students cancelled?

answer.worked:
Initially, 3 parts represent 12 staff.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=12\div3=4\\\text{Initial students}&=25\times4=100\end{align*}$$
After cancellations, 2 parts represent the same 12 staff.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=12\div2=6\\\text{Remaining students}&=15\times6=90\\\text{Students cancelled}&=100-90=10\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: At the last minute, 15 extra students and 15 extra staff join. The new ratio is $40:7$. How many students and staff were there to begin with?

answer.worked:
Adding equal numbers leaves the difference between students and staff unchanged. Express both ratios with a difference of 66 parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Initial ratio}&=25:3=75:9\\\text{New ratio}&=40:7=80:14\\\text{Initial difference}&=75-9=66\\\text{New difference}&=80-14=66\end{align*}$$
The increase is 5 parts for each group, representing 15 people.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=15\div5=3\\\text{Initial students}&=75\times3=225\\\text{Initial staff}&=9\times3=27\end{align*}$$
Check: $240:42=40:7$ after adding 15 to each group.

children.label: d
children.prompt: The ratio of male to female students is $8:7$ and the ratio of male to female staff is $4:5$. What fraction of the total are male?

answer.worked:
Use the equivalent students-to-staff ratio $75:9$, so each group can be divided into its male and female parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Male students}&=75\div(8+7)\times8\\&=40\\\text{Male staff}&=9\div(4+5)\times4\\&=4\\\text{Fraction male}&=\frac{40+4}{75+9}\\&=\frac{44}{84}\\&=\frac{11}{21}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Jessie is making fuel for her leaf blower by mixing petrol with oil.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Her current container has 4.1 litres of fuel mixed in a ratio of $40:1$ (petrol : oil).

How much petrol and how much oil are in this mixture?

answer.worked:
Total parts: $40+1=41$.

$$\begin{align*}41\text{ parts}&=4.1\text{ L}\\1\text{ part}&=4.1\div41=0.1\text{ L}\\40\text{ parts}&=40\times0.1=4\text{ L}\end{align*}$$

There are 4 L of petrol and 0.1 L of oil.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Jessie’s leaf blower manual states the correct mixing ratio should be $25:1$ (petrol : oil).

If she wants to correct her mixture and already has 4 litres of petrol, how much oil should be in the mixture in total?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}25\text{ parts}&=4\text{ L}\\1\text{ part}&=4\div25=0.16\text{ L}\end{align*}$$

The mixture needs 0.16 L of oil in total.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How much extra oil does Jessie need to add to her current mixture to achieve the correct ratio?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Extra oil}&=0.16-0.1\\&=0.06\text{ L}\\&=60\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$

Jessie needs to add 60 mL of oil.

inlines.text: Lily is making a drink by mixing water and cordial. She starts by making 5.4 L of drink using a ratio of
. However, the instructions say she should use the ratio of
. How much more cordial should she add to her current mixture so that the ratio is correct?

answer.worked:
Initially, water : cordial is $35:1$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Total parts} &= 35+1=36\\
36\text{ parts} &= 5.4\text{ L}\\
1\text{ part} &= 5.4\div36=0.15\text{ L}\\
\text{Water} &= 35\times0.15=5.25\text{ L}
\end{align*}$$
The water stays at 5.25 L. For the required ratio $20:1$:
$$\begin{align*}
20\text{ parts} &= 5.25\text{ L}\\
1\text{ part} &= 5.25\div20=0.2625\text{ L}\\
\text{Extra cordial} &= 0.2625-0.15=0.1125\text{ L}\\
\text{Extra cordial} &= 0.1125\times1000=112.5\text{ mL}
\end{align*}$$
Lily should add 112.5 mL of cordial.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{3}&=\frac{4}{1}\\2x&=12\\x&=6\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{3}&=\frac{5}{1}\\2x&=15\\x&=7.5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{3}&=\frac{6}{1}\\2x&=18\\x&=9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{6}&=\frac{6}{1}\\2x&=36\\x&=18\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4x}{6}&=\frac{6}{1}\\4x&=36\\x&=9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4x}{6}&=\frac{3}{1}\\4x&=18\\x&=4.5\end{align*}$$

Equivalent ratios show the same relationship between two quantities.
To make equivalent ratios, multiply or divide every part by the same number.

entries.description:
A fully simplified ratio has no fractions and no decimals.
• If there are decimals:
  1. Multiply each part by a power of 10 to get whole numbers.
  2. Divide by the highest common factor.
• If there are fractions:
  1. Rewrite the fractions with their lowest common denominator.
  2. Multiply by the denominator.
  3. Simplify the result, if needed.

entries.description: Finding Lengths in Scale Drawings

A scale drawing is a smaller or larger drawing of a real-life object.
Examples include maps, house plans, and scientific diagrams.
We call the real-life object the original, and the drawing the image.
Scales for scale drawings are written in simplified ratio notation:
image : original
Common forms are 1 : n and n : 1. When n > 1, 1 : n represents a reduction and n : 1 represents an enlargement.
A scale of 1:500 means every 1 unit on the drawing is 500 units in real life.
1. Set up a ratio table image : original
   a. The first row should be the given scale.
   b. The second row should be the given length and the length you want to find.
2. Find the unknown side by multiplying or dividing.
